Risk is any deviation from the project design intention that can result in unsafe operating conditions or unexpected difficulties during operation. v) The categories of potential hazards that have been predicted and considered during the HAZOP review are the following: - External and environmental hazards - Facility/interface hazards - Health hazards - Project implementation issues vi) Commercial risks (for example, cost overrun, delays, cashflows, payment terms, etc.) are not the study's objective and are not considered in this study. vii) HAZOP is an organized form of analysis that facilitates a systematic evaluation of the probable hazards associated with the specific process and operational issues that can affect the CCU and WGS plant. viii) For this study, the normal operating mode has been addressed. Startup/shutdown and abnormal operation issues have been considered deviations. Attachment-5: Hazard & Operability Review 3 DE-FE0031937 / 0006 ix) To conduct the Pre-HAZOP study, questions have been asked regarding the deviations to the process parameters to evaluate consequences from a design intent perspective at selected locations in the process flow. It is focused on identifying significant issues, particularly those which can significantly impact the plant's environment, health, and safety. The team’s comments have been recorded regarding each deviation as agreed upon by the team. The proposed recommendations from these discussions were noted on the worksheet as actions. During detailed engineering, these actions are needed to be considered. x) The worksheet developed for recording Pre-HAZOP findings was reviewed during each meeting. The team has chosen the deviations, and any condition, function, malfunction, or operation that can result from the deviation being evaluated has been noted in the Cause column. The Consequences column has been used to mention the resulting worst-case consequences from each cause if no safeguards are in place. In case of system safeguards are sufficient to protect the plant, such as instrumentation, alarms, shutdowns, relief valves, or operator action to mitigate the consequences are included in the design. System safeguards have been recorded in the Safeguards columns of the worksheet. If the available safeguards are insufficient to address the issue/protect the plant from the identified consequences, the team has decided that a change is warranted to improve safety or operability. Recommendations have been mentioned in the Recommendations column for a revisit during the FEED and construction phase. These changes can be in hardware, instrumentation, controls, or operating procedures. The HAZOP worksheet acts as a record of all the review sessions. xi) The team has also assigned the Hazard Category form I-IV depending on the significance of the causes and effects of the hazard.
